s1.syndrome_frame: Gradual onset of mild headaches with a mass in the parietal bone
salient_findings: Mild headaches of several months’ duration
19-mm mass in the left parietal bone
Lesion isointense to muscle on T1-weighted images with internal hyperintense foci
key_facts: Mild headaches of several months’ duration
Previous cranial MRI 4 years earlier showed no significant change in the lesion
Noncontrast CT of the head revealed a well-defined mass in the left parietal bone
Lesion centered in the diploic space with sparse but preserved trabeculae
Slight bony bulge without disruption of the inner or outer tables
Lesion isointense to muscle on T1-weighted images
Lesion with multiple internal hyperintense foci on T1-weighted images

shortlist.label: Hemangioma of bone
shortlist.why_kept: Well-defined mass in the diploic space with preserved trabeculae and isointense to muscle on T1-weighted images

shortlist.label: Intraosseous lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Lesion with multiple internal hyperintense foci on T1-weighted images, suggesting bone marrow fat

shortlist.label: Osteoma
shortlist.why_kept: Well-defined, 19-mm mass in the left parietal bone near the squamosal suture

shortlist.label: Fibrous dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Slight bony bulge without disruption of the inner or outer tables and heterogeneous signal on T2-weighted images

shortlist.label: Aneurysmal bone cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Restricted diffusion on MRI and presence of a well-defined mass in the parietal bone

raw.rationale: The lesion's appearance on MRI, being isointense to muscle on T1-weighted images with multiple internal hyperintense foci and heterogeneous signal on T2-weighted images, along with restricted diffusion, is consistent with a hemangioma of bone. The presence of a well-defined mass in the diploic space with preserved trabeculae and a slight bony bulge also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Intraosseous lipoma
rejected.why: Intraosseous lipomas typically appear hyperintense on T1-weighted images due to their high fat content, which is not the primary characteristic of this lesion.

rejected.label: Osteoma
rejected.why: Osteomas are typically small, well-defined bony growths that do not usually exhibit the complex signal characteristics seen on MRI in this case.

rejected.label: Fibrous dysplasia
rejected.why: Fibrous dysplasia often presents with a more ground-glass appearance on radiographs and a varied signal on MRI, not specifically matching the described lesion's characteristics.

rejected.label: Aneurysmal bone cyst
rejected.why: Aneurysmal bone cysts are typically expansile lesions with fluid-fluid levels on MRI, which were not described in this case.
